paragraphs.title: Jeremiah’s Release and the Choice Between Babylon and Judah

easy.explanation: Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, released Jeremiah from the chains on his hands.
easy.q: Who released Jeremiah from his chains?

answers: It fulfilled the word of the Lord
It was caused by a famine
easy.explanation: Nebuzaradan said that the Lord had brought the evil according as he had said.
easy.q: What did Nebuzaradan say about the destruction of Jerusalem and Judah?

easy.explanation: Jeremiah went to Gedaliah at Mizpah and dwelt with the people left in the land.
easy.q: To whom did Jeremiah go after he was released?

answers: To come to Babylon with him or remain in the land
To fight Babylon or flee to Egypt
To become a king or captain
medium.explanation: Nebuzaradan offered Jeremiah the choice of going with him to Babylon or remaining wherever he preferred in the land.
medium.q: What choice did Nebuzaradan offer Jeremiah?

medium.answer: Because they had sinned against the Lord and had not obeyed his voice.
medium.explanation: Nebuzaradan explained that the people’s sin and disobedience caused the destruction.
medium.q: According to verse 3, why had the destruction come upon the people?

answers: Stay behind or refrain from going
medium.explanation: In this context, “forbear” means Jeremiah could remain behind instead of going to Babylon.
medium.q: What does the word “forbear” mean in Nebuzaradan’s offer?

answers: Living in a city or living in a village
Going to Babylon or remaining in the land
Leading the army or leading the people
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah could go to Babylon with Nebuzaradan or remain in the land of Judah.
challenge.q: What was the main contrast in the choice given to Jeremiah?

answers: He chose to remain among the remnant in the land
He agreed to become governor under Babylon
He wanted to leave Judah immediately
challenge.explanation: Jeremiah went to Gedaliah and dwelt among the people who remained in the land.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Jeremiah’s going to Gedaliah?

answers: The destruction proved the prophecy false
The destruction fulfilled what had been spoken
challenge.explanation: Nebuzaradan said the Lord had done according as he had said, showing that the destruction fulfilled the spoken word.
challenge.q: What relationship between prophecy and destruction does Nebuzaradan describe?

paragraphs.title: Gedaliah’s Appointment and the Restoration of the Land’s Remnant

easy.explanation: The king of Babylon made Gedaliah governor over the cities and people left in Judah.
easy.q: Who appointed Gedaliah governor over the land?

answers: Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon
easy.explanation: Gedaliah told them to dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon so that it would be well with them.
easy.q: What did Gedaliah tell the people to do?

easy.explanation: Gedaliah told them to gather wine, summer fruits, and oil and put them in their vessels.
easy.q: What produce did Gedaliah tell the people to gather?

answers: They gathered wine and summer fruits in great abundance
medium.explanation: The Jews returned to Judah and gathered very much wine and summer fruits.
medium.q: What did the Jews who returned to the land do after coming to Gedaliah?

medium.answer: The people who were left after the others had been carried away captive.
medium.explanation: A remnant is what remains after a larger group has been removed or destroyed.
medium.q: What does “remnant” mean in the phrase “a remnant of Judah”?

answers: The people gathered produce, Gedaliah was appointed, and the commanders arrived
Gedaliah was appointed, people came to him, and he encouraged them to remain and gather produce
Johanan killed Ishmael, and then the Jews returned
medium.explanation: Gedaliah was appointed first, people came to him, and he encouraged them to stay, serve Babylon, and gather the land’s produce.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the events in these verses?

answers: They were expected to rebuild their lives in the land
They were preparing to leave for Babylon
challenge.explanation: The instruction to remain, work, and gather produce shows an attempt to restore ordinary life in the land.
challenge.q: What does the invitation to dwell in the land and gather its produce suggest about the remnant?

answers: They heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah over the remnant
Gedaliah ordered them to prepare for war
challenge.explanation: They heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah and had set Gedaliah over them.
challenge.q: Why did Jews from Moab, Ammon, Edom, and other countries return to Judah?

answers: Rebel against Babylon and gather weapons
Serve Babylon, remain in the land, and gather its produce
challenge.explanation: Gedaliah urged the people to serve the king of Babylon, dwell in the land, and gather its produce.
challenge.q: What policy did Gedaliah propose to allow the people to continue living in the land?

easy.explanation: Johanan and the commanders told Gedaliah that Ishmael had been sent to slay him.

answers: Baalis the king of the Ammonites
easy.explanation: The commanders said that Baalis, king of the Ammonites, had sent Ishmael.
easy.q: Who had sent Ishmael to kill Gedaliah?

easy.explanation: The text says that Gedaliah believed them not.
easy.q: How did Gedaliah respond to the warning?

medium.explanation: Johanan offered to go and slay Ishmael secretly so that no man would know it.
medium.q: What did Johanan offer to do to Ishmael?

medium.answer: So that Ishmael would not slay Gedaliah and cause all the Jews gathered there to be scattered.
medium.explanation: Johanan feared that Ishmael’s attack would scatter the people and cause the remnant in Judah to perish.
medium.q: Why did Johanan want Ishmael killed secretly?

answers: In a concealed way, without others knowing
medium.explanation: Johanan proposed acting secretly, so that no one would know what had been done.
medium.q: What does “secretly” mean in this passage?

answers: Johanan wanted immediate secret action, while Gedaliah rejected the warning
Johanan ignored the threat, while Gedaliah prepared for war
Both agreed that Ishmael was harmless
challenge.explanation: Johanan proposed secretly killing Ishmael, but Gedaliah refused because he did not believe the warning.
challenge.q: What was the difference between Johanan’s response and Gedaliah’s response to the threat?

answers: The scattering of all the Jews gathered to Gedaliah
The exile of the army commanders to Babylon
challenge.explanation: Johanan warned that the Jews could be scattered and the remnant in Judah could perish.
challenge.q: What broader danger did Johanan see beyond Gedaliah’s personal death?

answers: He believed Ishmael was loyal to him
He feared the king of Babylon
He thought Johanan was speaking falsely about Ishmael
challenge.explanation: Gedaliah answered, “Thou shalt not do this thing: for thou speakest falsely of Ishmael.”
challenge.q: Why did Gedaliah reject Johanan’s proposal?
